Name: spclt_improvement_no_reviews
Title: Structure-Preserving Contrastive Learning for Spatial Time Series: Improving a Rejected Paper
Short Hypothesis: The SPCLT paper proposes structure-preserving regularisers (topology + graph geometry) for contrastive learning of spatial time series and was rejected from ICLR 2025. Read the paper, run the experiments, identify weaknesses independently, and produce an improved publishable version.
Task:
You are improving a real rejected research paper. Produce an improved, publication-ready version.

STEP 1 — Download and read the paper source (first ~10 pages):
```bash
mkdir -p /app/paper_source && cd /app/paper_source
curl -sL 'https://arxiv.org/e-print/2502.06380' -o source.tar.gz
tar -xzf source.tar.gz
# Main tex file:
head -300 elsarticle-template-num.tex   # read intro, abstract, methods
```

STEP 2 — Clone the repo and understand the codebase:
```bash
cd /app && git clone https://github.com/Yiru-Jiao/spclt experiment_codebase
cd experiment_codebase && ls && cat README.md
```

STEP 3 — Based on your OWN assessment of the paper's weaknesses (do NOT look at OpenReview), design and run additional experiments to strengthen it, then write the improved paper.

EXPERIMENTAL RIGOR (non-negotiable):
- Before your FIRST submission: run at least one baseline and one new experiment — all numbers must be real
- Each subsequent version needs meaningful new content: new result, new baseline, new analysis, or fixing a critical reviewer-flagged issue (not just rephrasing)
- If a dataset/environment fails twice in 20 minutes: switch to a working alternative immediately (smaller dataset, different source, simpler setup)
- Check /data/ first — datasets may already be cached
- You have 6 hours — allocate ~30min literature, ~2-3h experiments, rest for writing/iteration
What_NOT_To_Do: Do not redesign the method from scratch. Do NOT resubmit a new version with only minor text polish — each version must show meaningful progress (new experimental result, new analysis, new baseline, or fixing a critical structural issue the reviewer flagged). Do NOT spend more than 20 minutes on any single dataset/environment issue — switch to a feasible working alternative. Do NOT stop after 1-2 submissions — submit at least 5 versions.
GPU_Note: RTX 5060 8GB VRAM available. Trains contrastive encoder across multiple UEA datasets with repeated runs. GPU significantly reduces runtime.
